meta.title: Synthetic Claim Denial Basics
meta.audience: New revenue operations team members (synthetic example)
objectives: Identify the three most common denial reasons in the synthetic claim set
Choose the right next step for a denied claim
Complete the corrected claim checklist before resubmitting
sources: Synthetic example: claims denial job aid outline, 2026-10-11
Synthetic example: team denial log summary (no patient data)

screens.title: Why Denials Matter
screens.body:
A denied claim delays payment. Most denials can be fixed in one pass when you read the code first.

This module takes about 12 minutes.

screens.title: The Three Common Reasons
screens.body: In the synthetic claim set, three reasons cause most denials.
bullets: Eligibility not confirmed for the date of service
Coding mismatch between the claim and the order

screens.title: Four Steps for Every Denial
screens.body: Follow the same four steps for every denial, in order.
screens.alt: Four steps in a row: 1 read the denial code, 2 check the claim data, 3 correct or appeal, 4 resubmit and track.

question.stem: Which of these is one of the three common denial reasons?

options.feedback: Yes. Authorization problems are one of the three common reasons.

options.text: The claim was printed in color
options.feedback: Print color does not affect claims. Look at authorization, eligibility and coding.
A slow portal delays your work but does not cause a denial.

screens.title: Correct or Appeal
screens.body: Correct the claim when the data was wrong. Appeal when the claim was right and the payer applied a rule in error.
bullets: Correct: fix the field and resubmit
Appeal: attach the supporting documents and file within the payer window

screens.title: A Denial Lands in Your Queue
screens.body: A claim comes back with an eligibility denial. The coverage check in the synthetic record shows active coverage on the date of service.

choices.text: Resubmit the same claim right away
choices.feedback: Resubmitting without a change usually gets the same denial. Check why the payer saw no coverage first.

choices.text: Confirm coverage with the payer, then correct the member details and resubmit
choices.feedback: Right. Confirm, correct the details that caused the mismatch, then resubmit and track it.
A write-off is the last step, not the first. Coverage was active, so the claim can be fixed.

screens.title: Practice the Checklist
screens.body: Choose every item that belongs on the corrected claim checklist.

question.stem: Which items do you check before resubmitting?

options.feedback: Yes. Confirm the reason for the denial is fixed.

options.text: The corrected claim indicator is set
options.feedback: Yes. The payer needs to know this replaces the first claim.

options.text: The claim is printed and filed
options.feedback: Not needed. Claims are tracked in the system, not on paper.
Yes. Set a follow-up so the claim does not stall.

screens.title: Summary
screens.body: Read the code, pick the step, use the checklist, and track the claim until it pays.
